markdown-linting-violations.name: markdown-linting-violations
markdown-linting-violations.description: Missing code language tags, emphasis as headings, missing blank lines around structures and horizontal rules
markdown-linting-violations.remediation: Add language tags (bash/text/json), use proper # headings, add blank lines around structures (headings, lists, code blocks, horizontal rules)

detectionRules.MD040: An OPENING code fence (``` followed by newline) with no language tag. A closing fence is always bare and is never tagged: CommonMark forbids an info string on it, and a tagged closer never closes its block (GRIP#7905)
detectionRules.MD036: Lines starting with ** or * containing : or structural content
detectionRules.MD022: Headings not surrounded by blank lines
detectionRules.MD022-HR: Horizontal rules (---) not surrounded by blank lines
detectionRules.MD031: Code fences not surrounded by blank lines
detectionRules.MD032: Lists not surrounded by blank lines

markdown-underscore-identifier.name: markdown-underscore-identifier
markdown-underscore-identifier.description: A snake_case identifier, a file name such as build_handcheck.py, or a key such as per_child, written bare outside code. CommonMark and GitHub never render this as italics, but some Markdown viewers do (the underscore opens emphasis mid-word), so GRIP wraps it in backticks regardless. markdownlint has no rule number for this: it is GRIP's own rule, named MD-US here so it has a name alongside the numbered rules it sits beside.
markdown-underscore-identifier.tokenImpact: n/a (a rendering defect for the operator, not a token-waste pattern)
markdown-underscore-identifier.remediation: Wrap the whole identifier, extension included, in backticks: per_person_sharing -> `per_person_sharing`; build_handcheck.py -> `build_handcheck.py`
markdown-underscore-identifier.implementation: lib/markdown_underscore_check.py (find_identifiers, fix_text) -- the one implementation the skill, the agent and /markdown-lint all use

examples.violation: The config uses per_person_sharing as a key.
examples.fix: The config uses `per_person_sharing` as a key.

neverTouched: link targets and image paths -- the (...) part of [text](target) and ![alt](src)
an already escaped underscore, e.g. per\_person
_italic_ and __bold__ emphasis markers (no underscore join inside a plain word)

detectionRules.MD-US: A run of word characters joined by one or more literal, unescaped underscores, outside any protected region, optionally followed by a dotted file extension. Not a markdownlint rule number -- markdownlint has no rule for this.
